stages.title: Recruiter screen
turns: dana
Dana Okafor (recruiter, Halden Robotics): Thanks for making time, Priya. Before we get into the role, what are you looking for in your next position?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): I want to own the motion-control stack end to end. At my current job at Kessler Automation I tune servo loops, but someone else decides the architecture.
dana
Dana Okafor (recruiter, Halden Robotics): That is exactly the scope of this role. What base salary are you targeting?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): I am targeting a base salary of $185,000 to $195,000. Equity matters less to me than base.
dana
Dana Okafor (recruiter, Halden Robotics): Understood. What is your notice period?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): My notice period is eight weeks, so the earliest I could start is November 30.
dana
Dana Okafor (recruiter, Halden Robotics): And location: the team sits in our Pittsburgh lab. Does that work?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): Yes. I live in Pittsburgh and I am happy to be on-site four days a week.
stages.scorecard: Strong yes from the screen. Clear motivation to own architecture, not just tuning. Base expectation $185k–$195k, notice period eight weeks (earliest start November 30), lives in Pittsburgh and fine with four days on-site.

stages.title: Technical interview
turns: marcus
Marcus Lee (hiring manager, Halden Robotics): Walk me through the last control loop you designed from scratch.
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): A cascaded position-velocity loop for a six-axis arm. I modelled the plant in MATLAB, then ran the loops on a TwinCAT PLC at 4 kHz.
marcus
Marcus Lee (hiring manager, Halden Robotics): Our cells need safety-rated motion. Have you worked with SIL 2 or PL d functions?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): I have integrated safe torque off, but I have not certified a safety function myself. A separate safety team owned that at Kessler.
marcus
Marcus Lee (hiring manager, Halden Robotics): How would you debug a loop that is stable in simulation but oscillates on the real arm?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): First check sample timing jitter and encoder resolution, then look for an unmodelled resonance with a frequency sweep before touching the gains.
stages.scorecard: Lean yes. Excellent loop design and a disciplined debugging method. Concern: no hands-on certification of safety-rated functions (SIL 2 / PL d); she would need the safety course in her first quarter.

stages.title: Values interview
turns: aiko
Aiko Sato (values interviewer, Halden Robotics): Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision.
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): We were shipping a firmware change without a hardware-in-the-loop test. I wrote up the risk, proposed a two-day test plan, and we ran it. It caught a sign error.
aiko
Aiko Sato (values interviewer, Halden Robotics): How do you like to work with junior engineers?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): Pairing on real bugs. I mentor two juniors now and we review each other's tuning notes every Friday.
aiko
Aiko Sato (values interviewer, Halden Robotics): Anything that changed since you spoke with Dana?
priya
Priya Raman (candidate): Yes, my manager agreed to shorten my notice, so I can now start on November 16 instead of November 30.
stages.scorecard: Strong yes. Raises risk in writing and proposes the fix; already mentors two juniors. Update: notice shortened, earliest start is now November 16 (was November 30).
